DEDR4782 supplies mā/māvu mango and DEDR4004 Tamil paḻam, Irula pammu/pāmu ripe fruit. Survey māva-pammu/māve-pammu/māva-pāmu/māve-paiṃmu and Tamil māmpaḻam are ordered mango + ripe-fruit compounds; the entire compound is preserved with its source spacing and diacritics.

DEDR5373 gives vāḻai/vāḻa and Kannada bāḻe banana; DEDR4004 gives Irula pammu/pāmu and Kannada paṇṇu fruit. Survey vā-/vē-/bāḷa-/bē- plus pammu/pāmu/paṇṇu-type banana responses are proposed contracted banana + ripe-fruit compounds. The contractions are comparative analyses, preserving the original complete response, rather than separately attested dictionary headwords.
DEDR754 gives Parji ūluvi plantain and DEDR4004 Parji pal ripe fruit. Survey ulu-pal is the ordered plantain + fruit compound, preserving the contracted first component.

DEDR5301 gives Kannada badaṇe/badane and Malayalam vaḻutina brinjal; DEDR1459 gives kāy/kāyi/kāyu fruit. These southern badaṇe/vadane + kāy survey eggplant responses are ordered brinjal + fruit compounds, preserving labial/medial voicing and vowels. DEDR’s Sanskrit comparison does not by itself determine the prehistory or transmission route of every lect form.

DEDR784 Tamil/Malayalam eṭṭu eight plus DEDR1479 kāl leg supports survey eṭṭukāli spider as eight + leg, with its ordinary nominal ending. Preserve the complete eight-legged designation as a compound.

DEDR2599 supplies cīvu sweep and related broom nouns; DEDR1147 Malayalam keṭṭu means tie/bundle. Survey cīva-keṭṭu broom is an ordered sweep/broom-material + bundle compound, preserving source spacing and gemination.

DEDR4616 explicitly gives Gadaba maginḍ sinḍ man/husband and maga sinḍu boy child; DEDR2594 independently gives sinḍ/cinḍu son. Survey magincindu/makindsind is an ordered male + son/child compound, preserving source consonants and final endings rather than linking the whole response to only one constituent.

DEDR1173 supplies gaṇḍu/gaṇḍ male and DEDR4616 supplies maga/magu/mog child/person. Survey gaṇḍu-maka/kaṇḍu-muga/gaṇa-mage/gan-mug is an ordered male + child/person compound, with source cluster reduction and final vowels retained. This is a comparative component analysis, not a claim that the entire compound is an indivisible inherited stem.

DEDR4395 and4616 explicitly give Kota pe-mog woman, female + child/person; Kannada peṇṇu/heṇṇu and magu supply the corresponding components. Survey pemmuh/pemug/yennu-magu preserves that ordered female + child/person construction and its source consonant notation.

DEDR399 explicitly documents Kodagu āŋuññi male child as āṇi-kuññi; DEDR1646 supplies Malayalam kuññu/kuñci infant and Kodagu kuññi child. Muthuvan/Kadar āṇ-kuñci/āŋguñci-type boy responses are comparative male + child compounds, with nasal-place assimilation and source final vowels retained.

DEDR4395 supplies peṇ female and DEDR1646 supplies Malayalam kuññu/kuñci child. Survey peŋguñci/paṇṇu-kuñci girl is an ordered female + child compound with ordinary nasal assimilation and source consonant/vowel notation preserved.

DEDR4395 supplies peṇ female and DEDR4198 piḷḷai/piḷḷa child. Survey peṇṇu-piḷḷe/paṇ-puḷḷe girl is an ordered female + child compound; source vowels and gemination are preserved. The University of Madras Tamil Lexicon also explicitly records peṇ-piḷḷai girl/woman/wife (https://agarathi.com/word/பெண்பிள்ளை).

DEDR4395(b) gives peṭṭai female/woman/girl and colloquial poṭṭacci, while DEDR4198 gives piḷḷai/piḷḷa child. Survey poṭṭa-/peṭṭa-piḷḷai/pulla/pulle girl is an ordered female + child compound with the source vowel and stop variants retained; subsection(b) is specified rather than silently treating it as the simple peṇ form.

DEDR4395 explicitly gives Kodagu poṇṇa-āḷi woman and supplies the peṇ female stem; DEDR399 supplies āḷ person. Kudiya peṇṇāl and Urali peŋgāḷi woman/wife/girl are proposed ordered female + person compounds with the survey intervocalic/nasal consonants and final vowels retained.

Ordered weight + absence components: DEDR1404 supplies kaṉam heaviness and DEDR2559 supplies illa/illā not existing, including ordinary negative adjectival forms. The survey whole expressions mean light, literally without weight; their source contractions and endings are preserved. DEDR1404 expressly notes influence from Sanskrit ghana on the kaṉa heavy family; that contact qualification is retained, and no unsupported immediate donor is asserted.

Ordered weight + reduced/less components: DEDR1404 gives kaṉam heaviness and1851 kuṟai/kuṟavu diminish/deficiency/less. These kanam-kuranna/kurava responses mean light through diminished weight, retaining the inflected/adjectival second constituent. DEDR1404 expressly notes influence from Sanskrit ghana on the kaṉa heavy family; that contact qualification is retained, and no unsupported immediate donor is asserted.

Ordered small + weight components: DEDR2594 gives ciṉṉa small and1404 kaṉa heavy/kaṉam weight. The whole survey ciṉṉa-kaṉa response means light through small weight; neither constituent alone is treated as the complete word. DEDR1404 expressly notes influence from Sanskrit ghana on the kaṉa heavy family; that contact qualification is retained, and no unsupported immediate donor is asserted.

Ordered weight + little components: DEDR1404 kaṉa heavy/kaṉam weight and2041 koñcam/koñca little supply the two lexical constituents of gaṉa-koñjatu light. Preserve the source voiced stops and adjectival ending. DEDR1404 expressly notes influence from Sanskrit ghana on the kaṉa heavy family; that contact qualification is retained, and no unsupported immediate donor is asserted.

Ordered river + margin components: DEDR5159 explicitly gives āṟu river with oblique āṟṟu-, and1060 gives Malayalam/Tamil ōram margin/edge. Mannan āttōram is proposed as the corresponding river-bank expression, retaining the source elicited river gloss and its broader metonymic interpretation rather than silently relabelling the record.

Ordered arrow + bow components: DEDR178 gives Malayalam/Tamil ampu arrow and5422 gives vil/villu bow. The Muthuvan ambum-villu(m) rainbow expressions transparently coordinate arrow and bow with grammatical -um, which adds no separate lexical ancestor. Preserve the elicited rainbow meaning and exact constituent order.

Ordered sky + bow components: DEDR5381 gives vān/vāṉam sky and5422 vil/villu bow. Irula vǣṉavillu rainbow is proposed as sky-bow, retaining the survey fronted vowel and linking medial vowel; the complete expression receives both components.

Ordered big + watercourse components: DEDR5276 explicitly gives Malayalam valiya great/big and1041 ōṭa watercourse. Muthuvan veliya-ōḍa/veliyōḍa river expresses a large watercourse, retaining the source contraction and vowels.

Ordered big + river + margin components: DEDR5276 explicitly gives Malayalam valiya great/big and Kodagu ballyë great;5159 gives āṟu river with āṟṟu- oblique;1060 gives ōram margin/side. Mannan baliya-āttōram is a large-river-bank expression elicited as river; preserve that survey gloss and make the metonymic bank interpretation explicit.

Ordered come + be components: DEDR5270 explicitly gives Gondi vā-/vāy- come. Survey vā-si-ma- responses contain that lexical come root followed by the separately identified auxiliary; their full elicited forms are retained. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered die + be components: DEDR2426 gives Gondi sāy- die, with sās- past and hā- dialect variants. Survey sā-si-ma- responses retain the intransitive death root and an auxiliary, rather than being treated as single underived death stems. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered drink + be components: DEDR600 explicitly gives Gondi un-/unḍānā drink. These un-jege-/un-ji-ma- responses preserve that drinking root plus a separately identified auxiliary; the source drink gloss distinguishes them from sleep3291. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered give + be components: DEDR2598 explicitly gives Gondi sī-/hī-/ī- give. Survey sī-si-ma- responses preserve the lexical giving root and an auxiliary, with all source tense/person endings retained. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered go + be components: DEDR2781 explicitly gives Gondi han-/an-/son- go. These han-dzi-/han-ji-/han-ci-ma- responses preserve that go root followed by an auxiliary; longer forms with extra unresolved rhotic material are excluded. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered strike/kill + be components: DEDR2602 explicitly gives Gondi jīānā strike and (W.) beat/kill. The survey jī-si-ma- response uses that root rather than the separate jak- killing family2831. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered see + be components: DEDR2735 explicitly gives Gondi hūṛ-/hūr-/ūṛ- see. These hura-/hur-/ur-si-ma- responses retain the seeing root with its source rhotic/vowel variants plus an auxiliary. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered fly + be components: DEDR4020 explicitly gives Gondi pari- fly of birds. Survey pari-si-ma- preserves that lexical flight verb followed by an auxiliary. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered speak + be components: DEDR5310 explicitly gives Gondi vaṛk- and vank- speak/talk. These vaṛk-/vaŋk-si-ma- responses retain those dialect stems and the following auxiliary; their complete source forms are preserved. DEDR4778 supplies Gondi man-/matt- be/remain as the second component. Construction checked: [Southern Gondi grammar](https://www.gondwana.in/sites/www.gondwana.in/files/pdf-files/SGondi%20%28Aheri%29%20Grammar%20final%202000%20%28Unicode%29.pdf), pp.24–25; this is a comparison across survey lects, not a claim that every response is Aheri.

Ordered fire + kindle/burn components: DEDR1514 explicitly gives Gondi kis fire and4801 mās- kindle/burn transitively. The parenthetical survey (kisu)māsa response contains both lexical constituents; preserve the optional/parenthetical fire noun rather than treating the whole response as only a māsa stem.
DEDR3268(b) explicitly analyses Kurux tīnī bee as honey + fly, and533 repeats tīn+ī. The survey tini bee is represented by those ordered lexical components, preserving the complete source form.

Ordered honey + fly: DEDR3268(b) gives southern tēn/tēnu honey, and533 explicitly gives ĀlKu./PālKu. īpi and Irula īppi fly. Survey Betta Kurumba ṭænu-yippi bee transparently retains both constituents and its linking glide.

Ordered honey + insect: DEDR3268(b) explicitly gives Kannada jēnu/tēnu honey and4312 Kannada puẓu/puẓa insect, corresponding to the Kannada h/u- form after regular initial weakening. The survey jenu/dzenu/ḍenu + uḷuvu/uḷā bee responses retain both lexical constituents; the generic insect word is not confused with the separate wood-worm entry700.

Ordered sesame + oil: DEDR854 explicitly gives Tamil eṇ ṇey gingelly oil and related Malayalam eṇṇa/Kannada eṇṇe, while3746 gives ney oil. These lexicalized eṇṇey/eṇṇa/eṇṇe survey responses are analysed with both historical constituents; their generalized survey gloss oil and all dialect transcriptions remain unchanged.

Ordered sesame + oil: DEDR3720 gives Konda nū sesamum, and3746 gives Konda niyu oil and explicitly analyses Telugu nūne as *nū + ney. Konda nūne oil is compared as the corresponding lexicalized compound; the survey general oil gloss is retained.
Ordered upper + house: DEDR5086 gives mēl above/upper and5393 vīṭu house. Kurumba melviḍɨ roof transparently contains both lexical constituents; its elicited roof meaning is retained.
Ordered upper + roof: DEDR5086 gives mēl above/upper and1904 kūrai/kūra roof/thatch. Irula melkūra roof retains both constituents.

Ordered roof + ridge: DEDR1904 gives kūrai/kūra roof and4888 mukaṭu ridge/top of a roof. Eravallan kūramugaḍɨ roof contains both nouns; retain the source general roof gloss for this ridge compound. The external crown/diadem comparison in4888 is not treated as an established immediate borrowing route.

Ordered inside + hand: DEDR7 explicitly gives Tamil akaṅkai/aṅkai, Kannada aṅ-gey and Kodagu aŋgay palm of hand, with2023 kai/kay hand. Alu Kurumba aŋgāźɨ and Betta Kurumba aŋgiye palm preserve the corresponding contracted compound and dialectal consonants.

Ordered inside + hand: DEDR698 gives uḷ/uḷḷam inside/interior and2023 kai/kay hand. Survey uḷḷankai/aḷḷamkay/uḷḷāŋāy palm transparently combines the interior term and hand, with nasal sandhi retained. Current698 includes inside in its gloss; this use does not claim that the unrelated house responses belong there.

Ordered ground + gram: DEDR3676 nilam/nela earth/ground and1120 kaṭalai/kaṭala gram. Survey nila-/nela-kaḍala(i) groundnut transparently contains both constituents; its modern groundnut designation is retained as a compound, not conflated with the botanical gram referent of1120.
Ordered root + gram: DEDR5535 vēr root and1120 kaṭalai/kaḍale gram. Survey vēr-kaḍale/kaḍalai groundnut preserves both constituents of the modern crop name.

Ordered gram + nut/pod: DEDR1120 gives kaṭalai/kaḍale gram and1459 kāy/kāyi fruit/nut/pod. Survey kaḍala-kāy/kaḍale-kāi/kaḍlai-kai groundnut retains both constituents; the homepage Kannada kaḍalekāyi groundnut attestation supports the lexical extension.

Ordered round + tuber: DEDR664(a) gives uruḷai/uruḷa anything round and uruṇṭa round;1578 gives kiẓaṅku/kiẓaṅṅu esculent tuber, explicitly including potato. These survey uruḷa-/uraṇḍa- plus kiyaṅgu/kisaṅgu/keŋgu/kaŋgu potato compounds retain both lexical constituents, with source dialect consonants and vowels preserved.

Ordered round + fruit/tuber designation: DEDR664(a) gives uruṇṭa round and1459 kāy fruit/pod. Survey Urali urunḍakā potato retains this transparent shape-plus-produce name; do not replace the elicited potato referent by the general component meanings.
Ordered pepper + fruit/pod: DEDR4867 miḷaku/muḷaku pepper/chilli and1459 kāy fruit. Survey muḷakay/moḷakay chilli retains both historical lexical constituents and its source crop meaning.

Ordered big/elder + elder brother: DEDR5276 gives Malayalam valiya big/great and131 aṇṇan elder brother. Muthuvan baliyāṇṇan older brother retains both lexical constituents, with source initial b and vowel length.
Ordered small/young + child: DEDR1646 Malayalam kuñci/kuññi young/small/infant and4198 piḷḷa child. Mannan kuñjipuḷḷa child preserves both constituents.
Ordered small + child: DEDR1646 explicitly gives Kota kun small and4616 Kota mog child. Survey kun mug child is a transparent same-language compound; both source words and spacing are retained.

Ordered girl + child: DEDR364 explicitly gives Konda ayli daughter/girl and2149 koṛo female child, plural koṛok. These survey ayli koṛo/ayli koṛok responses retain both lexical constituents and the source woman gloss, including the plural form; the proposed analysis does not silently turn the prompt into girl.

Ordered male + child components, comparing the contracted Tamil formation. Sri Lanka Educational Publications Department, Tamil11, printed p.112 (https://noolaham.net/project/795/79443/79443.pdf), visually verified, explicitly pairs āmpiḷai with āṇpiḷḷai in its colloquial/standard table. DEDR399 supplies āṇ male and4198 piḷḷai child. Survey contractions preserve these components; source vowel/rhotic variants remain unchanged, and borrowing versus shared formation across varieties is not resolved by this component analysis. See tamil-contracted-kinship-evidence.md.

DEDR4395 supplies peṇ female and4198 piḷḷai child. Ordered stand + be auxiliary: DEDR3675 Gondi nil-/nillā stand and4778 man- remain/be. Survey nilliman stand retains both verb stems; Gondi compound/auxiliary constructions are documented in Southern Gondi (Aheri) Grammar pp24–25.
Ordered stand + be: DEDR3675 Kannada nil with nind- participial/past stem and480 iru be/remain. Survey nīndīru preserves the nindi-iru sequence; both lexical stems are represented.

Ordered sit + be: DEDR1728 Kannada kuntu/kūtu having sat down and480 iru be/remain/sit. Survey Betta Kurumba kūtnu īr explicitly retains two words, with the first a sitting participial form and the second the be auxiliary.
Ordered sit + reflexive auxiliary: DEDR1835 Kannada kuḷir/kuḷḷu sit and2151 Kannada koḷḷu, modern imperative kō, reflexive auxiliary. Survey kuḷitiko retains the sitting participle plus kō.
Ordered sit + reflexive auxiliary: DEDR1728 Kannada kūtu having sat down and2151 koḷḷu, modern imperative kō, reflexive auxiliary. Survey kūtuko retains both constituents.

Ordered stand + reflexive auxiliary: DEDR3675 Kannada nil with nilt-/nind- stems and2151 koḷḷu, modern imperative kō, reflexive auxiliary. Survey nīḷṭuko/nintiko preserve the standing stem plus kō, with source dental/retroflex spellings retained.
